title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1RC1RE_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RF0RF_0RA0LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1RC1RE_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RF0RF_0RA0LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At a left turn the tape is 0 1^n 0 followed by blocks of ones of odd length (1, 3, 5, …) separated by single 0s. The block 1^n is always 3 mod 4 and grows by multiples of 4; it is half of the tape (1,231 of 2,299 cells at 2.9·106 steps). The odd blocks on the right are rewritten every round trip, without visible order. Five shift rules of the sweeps are proved in Lean.
Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (10,000 by the kernel alone); the C simulator finds none in 10<sup>9</sup>.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: A with 0 under the head, 0 right, 1 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 43,516 cells have been visited and 38,421 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.5). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501).

claims.title: The sweep rules
claims.text: Shift rules of the two sweeps, for every repeat count and any tape around: F crosses ones going right (3 steps a cell) and D going left (1 step a cell), F erases the ones of (01)^n, D turns each 1110 into 1101 and F each 0111 into 1110.

claims.title: The left block
claims.text: At every left turn the tape starts 0 1^n 0 with n = 3 mod 4 (3, 7, 11, 15, 23, …, 1,231 at 2.9·106 steps); n grows by 4 to 20 at some round trips and stays the same at others.

claims.title: Odd blocks
claims.text: Right of the big block, the blocks of ones at a left turn have odd length (at 2.9·10<sup>6</sup> steps: 148 of length 1, 52 of 3, 38 of 5, 16 of 7, …, and one of 6, the only even one).

claims.title: The halt needs B>0 1
claims.text: The only halting transition C1 is reached only from B>0 1. In the first 109 steps B reads a 0 29,488,351 times, never with a 1 on its right.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. How the right region feeds the counter (each growth of n by 4k), and whether its rewriting can put a 1 right of a B on a 0, are not understood.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 43,516 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.5). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501).
After 109 steps the tape spans 43,516 cells (16,876 left of the start, 14,974 right), with a density of 1s of 0.883.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A counter and a garden
html: At a left turn the tape reads 0 1^n 0 1^a 0 1^b 0 … with n = 3 mod 4 and a, b, … odd. The big block grows by 4 to 20 cells at a time and stays about half of the tape.

sections.heading: Rules proved in Lean
html:
rulefromtowhat it does
f_onesL 1 F> (1)^n RL (1)^n 1 F> RRightward: F crosses a block of ones (3 steps a cell).
d_onesL (1)^n D> 1 RL D> 1 (1)^n RLeftward: D crosses a block of ones.
f_01L F> (01)^n RL (00)^n F> RRightward: F erases the ones of a run of 01.
d_1110L (1110)^n D> 1 RL D> 1 (1101)^n RLeftward: D turns each 1110 into 1101.
f_0111L 0 F> (0111)^n RL (1110)^n 0 F> RRightward: F, a 0 behind it, turns each 0111 into 1110.

sections.heading: Where a halt would come from
html: It halts from B>0 1: B reads a 0 about 29 million times in 109 steps, always with a 0 on its right. No proof that this always holds is known.

summary: A unary counter and a chaotic garden: the left half is one block of ones that grows by multiples of 4, the right half blocks of ones of odd length separated by single 0s that keep being rewritten.
family: unary counter beside a chaotic region of odd blocks

sections.heading: How it works
paragraphs: The left half of the tape is a single block of ones, a unary counter: its length is always 3 mod 4 and it grows by 4 to 20 cells at some round trips. The right half is blocks of ones of odd length separated by single 0s, rewritten every round trip.
The sweeps cross the counter quickly (rules proved in Lean); all the irregular work happens on the right. A halt needs B on a 0 with a 1 to its right, which has not happened in 10<sup>9</sup> steps.
